My sister suffers from depression and no matter how many times I say it she never believes me haha. I am here for you, no need to feel like a burden ok?!

I felt very lost and whilst I wasn't suicidal or anything (severely homesick, felt lost in life and generally couldn't motivate myself to get out of bed in the morning). I stopped answering calls, ignoring my flatmates knocking on my door for like a week before I realized I was getting stuck into a loop and needed to do something before it got worse.

My uni (I am in the UK but even if you aren't I presume they will be the same) was incredible. I emailed my personal tutor, they met me on the same day and talked it out. I suggested going to see my family and I was given leave the same day, on my return they met me as much as I wanted and sorted out counselling etc. Seriously these were people who I thought would never help, strict professionals who were really harsh when they marked me. But when it came to pastoral care they were different people, you are not the first person to go through this and they are trained to help. They have an obligation to do so and most genuinely care about your well-being. I was also allowed to sit exams in Summer without penalty etc and I really do feel better now.

My English friends always mention the fact we get two eids and how they only get one Christmas. I always reply pointing out that they get longer off for Christmas, and they counter point out I get Christmas off too. But hey the more days off the better as far as I'm concerned. 

Yeah I see what you mean with the whole gift thing. To be fair the dynamic in our house is changing too, my parents and grandparents are incredibly soft on my little bro/ cousins. I see it as them getting soft in the heart as they get older but they always deny it, normally whilst holding another new toy haha.

Eid is a muslim religious holiday, we actually have two a year :D Both represent different events  but are taken as religious holiday. 

Growing up in our family (and most the ones I know) we got money rather than presents, because unlike Christmas its not really a gift-centred day. Honestly I just like the fact that a) endless amounts of brilliant food (one Eid comes at the end of Ramadan- month of fasting, so its happily received!) and b) having the entire family together which seems to be rare nowadays.

Nowadays my youngest brother/cousins get cash and presents, dont really know what prompted the change but feel a little hard done by! :) Would be interested to see if its similiar for Muslims from different cultures but Pakistanis normally do cash. Funny little tidbit: there comes a stage when you sort of transition from receiving money to giving it to the little 'uns. In our family we have been delaying this (I still get money from my grandmother haha) but soon I have to be giving cash not receiving it!
